## 2.1 — CSG - an architectural object as instructions

**Introduced:** Week 2 — Sep 1 · **Due:** Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time · **Weight:** 10%

**Present:** One 17 x 11 inch sheet: precedent, numbered diagrams/instructions and final view; editable model.

### Purpose

Reinterpret the main form of a real architectural project as a short, understandable sequence of solid operations.

### What you will learn

- Navigate the basic Geometry Nodes or Grasshopper interface: connect nodes, identify inputs and outputs, and change a value.
- Move, rotate and scale geometry; understand union, subtraction and intersection.
- Break an architectural object into an ordered list of instructions that someone else can follow.

### What to do

- Choose a documented real project. Credit the project, architect and image source; identify the main forms you will simplify.
- Build an editable model from basic solids and transformations. Demonstrate union, subtraction and intersection; a small supporting comparison is acceptable if one operation is unnecessary in the main object.
- Explain the construction in about six to nine diagram steps. Match each step to a short instruction in ordinary language; formal code is not required.
- Use BIG-style graphics: white building masses, restrained color for changes or operations, clear outlines and simple line weights. Show context or vegetation in the final view.
- Name or separate objects when it helps explain the sequence. Use the [BIG-style diagram tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Y5Rn3bDL5s) in Resources.

### What to submit

- **Presentation:** one 17 x 11 inch landscape sheet, `Lastname_Firstname_P2a.pdf`.
- **On the sheet:** a small credited precedent image; about six to nine numbered construction diagrams; matching numbered instructions; and a final architectural view with context. Keep each instruction beside its diagram.
- **Operations:** make the transformations and Boolean operations legible. If an operation is demonstrated outside the main sequence, place the small comparison on this same sheet.
- **Editable model:** include `.blend`, or `.gh` with its referenced `.3dm`, plus external dependencies. Keep the construction steps and useful controls accessible.
- **Package:** `Lastname_Firstname_P2a/`. Open the model from the submission folder and confirm it reproduces the final view. Instructions may be plain language; no separate code document is required.

### What we assess

- Can you explain and change the construction sequence? Are the transformations and Boolean operations used intentionally? Does the sheet communicate the architectural interpretation clearly?
- Digital rubric: understanding 30%, communication 30%, technical execution 25%, exploration 15%.


<a id="p2b"></a>

## 2.2 — 3D printing - from model to layers

**Introduced:** Week 3 — Sep 8 · **Due:** Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time · **Weight:** 5%

**Present:** One CSG print; photograph and annotated slicer documentation PDF; editable geometry, print mesh and slicer settings/project.

### Purpose

Prepare and print your CSG object, using the slicer to understand how the machine will build it.

### What you will learn

- Recognize the slicer workspace, object placement, settings, supports, estimates and layer preview.
- Understand layers, walls, infill, adhesion, orientation, overhangs and bridging.
- Connect common print problems to a setting or geometry decision.

### What to do

- Check units and size, choose an orientation and inspect the layer preview before printing.
- Use a strategy to avoid or reduce supports: reorient the object, separate it into parts or adjust overhangs. Bridging is acceptable when the test or preview supports it.
- Identify the settings that matter for your object: layer height, walls, infill, adhesion and supports. Explain your choices briefly rather than listing every software option.
- Keep the assembled object within 60 mm on each axis and within the existing 200 g filament allowance, including tests and failed attempts.
- Document a problem and response, or an anticipated problem checked in the preview. Follow the FabLab workflow.

### What to submit

- **Physical outcome:** one assembled CSG print within 60 mm on each axis. The recorded midterm submission is an upload of print photographs to Teams, not a new physical hand-in.
- **Documentation:** `Lastname_Firstname_P2b.pdf` with an overall photograph of the finished object, an annotated slicer setup view and an annotated layer-preview view. Add a detail or failure photograph when it helps explain the result.
- **Explain briefly:** object dimensions; orientation or part splitting; layer height, walls, infill, adhesion and support choices; and one problem/test and your response. Use existing CSG documentation or the course template; no additional polished process sheet is required.
- **Machine/source files:** editable geometry, exported print mesh (`.stl` or `.3mf`) and the saved slicer project where supported; otherwise include the settings in the documentation.
- **Package:** `Lastname_Firstname_P2b/`. Check units, exported dimensions and that the documented settings match the printed result. Do not submit only a mesh or only photographs.

### What we assess

- Preparation and fabrication strategy 30%; fabrication quality 30%; visual documentation 25%; testing and revision 15%. Explain what the slicer shows and what you learned from the result.


**Ungraded checkpoints:**

- Week 6 — Sep 29: Before you queue the print, check the geometry, units, orientation and sliced preview.
